claim_summary: TradingAgents contributes a role-specialized, feedback-driven LLM workflow for financial decision support, combining structured reports, debate, trading decisions, and risk review.

claim_evidence.quote: In this work, we address these key limitations of existing models by introducing a system that overcomes these challenges. First, our framework bridges the gap by simulating the multi-agent decision-making processes typical of professional trading teams.

modules.name: Structured report-based shared communication
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK is no: this shared state/report protocol does not itself encode an investment objective or validation criterion, and its state/action semantics need not be redesigned for a different task. R3_2 GTS is no: it manages agent communication state without temporal-order, window, frequency, unit, or information-availability assumptions. R3_3 GH is yes: it organizes execution state and communication.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - state/report communication does not encode a task objective or criterion
R3_2_GTS:no - no temporal semantics in the communication mechanism
R4:Memory and Context; Planning and Orchestration

evidence.quote: Our model introduces a structured communication protocol to govern agent interactions. By clearly defining each agent’s state, we ensure that each role only extracts or queries the necessary information, processes it, and returns a completed report.

modules.name: Role-specialized investment workflow
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK is yes: the workflow produces buy/sell/hold decisions and applies investment and portfolio-risk criteria. Counterfactual: changing task family changes the temporal state, action space, trader role, and risk criteria, so these must be redesigned. R3_2 GTS is not selected because TSK is the first matching layer.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - investment decision objective and risk criteria are embedded

evidence.quote: Two researchers represent opposing perspectives: one bullish and one bearish. They engage in natural language dialogue for n rounds, as determined by the debate facilitator agent. At the conclusion, the facilitator reviews the debate history, selects the prevailing perspective, and records it as a structured entry in the communication protocol.

temporal_validity.quote: Agents make decisions based solely on data available up to each trading day, ensuring no future data is used (eliminating look-ahead bias).

decision_utility.quote: Cumulative Return (CR), Annualized Return (AR), Sharpe Ratio (SR), and Maximum Drawdown (MDD) (formulations in Appendix S1.2).

notes: The paper evaluates financial decision utility through returns and risk metrics; it does not report a separate task-output accuracy measure or runtime operation/failure validity check.
